title: A parameter in a reduced local curve localizes to the total fraction ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring (with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$), reduced (having no nonzero nilpotent elements), and of Krull dimension exactly one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A nonzerodivisor is an element $t$ such that $tr=0$ implies $r=0$ for every $r\in R$. Let $T$ be its set of nonzerodivisors, and $Q=T^{-1}R$ its total ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. For an ideal $I$, write $\sqrt I=\{x\in R: x^n\in I\text{ for some integer }n\geq1\}$. There exists $f\in\mathfrak m$ which is a nonzerodivisor and belongs to no minimal prime ideal (a prime containing no strictly smaller prime), such that $\sqrt{fR}=\mathfrak m$ and the canonical $R$-algebra map $R_f\to Q$ is an isomorphism, where $R_f$ is localization at the powers of $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0C3R, lemma-pre-pre-delta-invariant, existence assertion and equivalence with condition (5) for a reduced ring

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters] to the given Noetherian local ring with $d=1$. Its single parameter is an element $f\in\mathfrak m$ with $\sqrt{fR}=\mathfrak m$. We retain this particular $f$ for all subsequent steps.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, (1) implies (3), specialized to dimension one; the existence assertion used in Tag 0C3R

proof.text: Every prime $\mathfrak p$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$: if $x\in\mathfrak p$ lay outside $\mathfrak m$, [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion] would make $x$ a unit and force $1\in\mathfrak p$. If $\mathfrak p\ne\mathfrak m$ were not minimal, some prime $\mathfrak q$ would satisfy $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak m$, contradicting dimension one by [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Thus every prime other than $\mathfrak m$ is minimal. Moreover $\mathfrak m$ is not minimal: otherwise every prime contained in it would equal it, leaving no chain of length one, again contradicting dimension exactly one. Finally, if a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ contained $f$, it would contain $\sqrt{fR}$, since $x^n\in\mathfrak p$ implies $x\in\mathfrak p$ by induction using primality. Step 1 would give $\mathfrak m\subseteq\mathfrak p$, hence $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$, a contradiction. Therefore $f$ lies in no minimal prime.

source.place: Tags 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring, and 00KE, definition-Krull; elementary prime-chain argument underlying Tag 0C3R, (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Since $R$ is reduced, [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes] applies. The avoidance proved in step 2 says exactly that $f$ is a nonzerodivisor, so $f\in T$. Products of nonzerodivisors are nonzerodivisors: if $abx=0$, first cancel $a$, then $b$. Also $1\in T$, so $T$ is multiplicative and $f^n\in T$ for every integer $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 00EW, lemma-reduced-ring-sub-product-fields, (3); elementary cancellation for products and powers

proof.text: Using the fraction constructions in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] with $M=R$, define $\alpha:R_f\to Q$ by $\alpha(r/f^n)=r/f^n$, now with denominator $f^n\in T$. If $r/f^n=r\prime/f^m$ in $R_f$, then $f^k(rf^m-r\prime f^n)=0$ for some $k\geq0$. The same equality, with multiplier $f^k\in T$, proves equality in $Q$. Thus $\alpha$ is well defined. The displayed addition and multiplication formulas in these definitions show that it preserves addition, multiplication and $1$, and it sends $r/1$ to $r/1$. It is therefore precisely the canonical $R$-algebra map in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00CO, definition-localization, and the construction before Tag 07JZ, definition-localization-module; fraction formulas

proof.text: For each $s\in T$ we claim that $f^n=sa$ for some $a\in R$ and integer $n\geq0$. If $s$ is a unit, take $n=0$ and $a=s^{-1}$. Otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion] gives $s\in\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-zerodivisors-union-minimal-primes], $s$ belongs to no minimal prime. Step 2 then implies that the only prime containing $sR$ is $\mathfrak m$. Apply the radical-intersection clause of [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] to $sR$: its radical is $\mathfrak m$. Since $f\in\mathfrak m$, the definition of radical gives $f^n\in sR$ for some $n\geq1$, that is, $f^n=sa$ for some $a\in R$. This proves the claim also for nonunits.

source.place: Tags 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring; 00EW, lemma-reduced-ring-sub-product-fields, (3); 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, (7); explicit denominator argument for condition (5) of Tag 0C3R

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is injective: if $\alpha(r/f^n)=0$, the zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $t\in T$ with $tr=0$, hence $r=0$ by the definition of $T$, and consequently $r/f^n=0$ in $R_f$ by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. It is surjective: for any fraction $r/s\in Q$, choose $n,a$ from step 5 with $f^n=sa$. Then $\alpha(ra/f^n)=r/s$, since the cross-multiplied difference $(ra)s-rf^n$ is zero (multiplier $1\in T$). Thus $\alpha$ is a bijective $R$-algebra homomorphism; its inverse preserves the operations by applying injectivity to their images, so it is an $R$-algebra isomorphism. Together with steps 1--3, this gives every clause for the same element $f$.
